subject: Post-call: grounding checklist, retriever choices & eval assets for Acme BioSystems
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jackson <sarah.jackson@acmebio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: grounding checklist, retriever choices & eval assets for Acme BioSystems

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + proposed next steps so we have a clear pilot path.

Summary of call
- Primary goal: make search + assistant answers reliably grounded on Acme SOPs, papers, and instrument manuals (sensitive, PII allowed only in redacted form).
- Main risks you raised: hallucination on similar assay names, stale SOP versions, and retrieval recall for short procedural snippets.
- Success metrics you want to track in the pilot: grounding precision @ top-1, answer fidelity (binary correctness on 200 prompt checks), and latency target <= 400ms p95 for single-question queries.

Recommended evaluation approach (pilot scope)
1) Data & prompt set: we requested an initial sample set — I attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (200 prompts, mix of fact lookup and step-by-step procedural). Please add any redaction notes before we ingest.
2) Baselines to run: two retrieval configs + two reranker options + two generator variants. We recommend: 
   - Retriever A: hybrid BM25 + dense (FAISS flat) using embedding model text-embedding-3-small; chunk size 512 tokens.
   - Retriever B: dense-only (IVF) with 768-d vectors, chunk size 256, recall-focused.
   - Reranker options: a lightweight cross-encoder (distil-cross-enc-1.2) and a domain-finetuned cross-encoder (if you provide 300 labeled pairs later).
   - Generator models: redwood/long-lite-13b-q8 (faster, lower-cost) and an L2-13B open variant for quality comparison.
3) Benchmarks we'll produce: grounding precision@1/3/5, answer fidelity (binary pass/fail vs reference), exact-match for short facts, and latency/cost per query. Baseline CSV attached (baseline_benchmarks.csv).

Security/data handling
- For the pilot we'll use our private deployment mode (VPC). No raw logs will be shared without your explicit OK — we can enable PII redaction and token-level retention policy per your legal.

Next steps / asks from Acme
- Confirm we can ingest the attached prompt set as-is or send a redacted version by EOD Thu (2027-04-28).
- Share an example doc with the instrument manual (PDF stub or Drive link) so we can validate chunking heuristics.
- Quick follow-up: can we book a 45-min session next week to walk the eval script and agree on pass/fail thresholds? Here are proposed slots: Tue 10–11am, Wed 3–4pm, Thu 9–10am PT.

I'll loop Karthik on technical retrieval and reranker specifics — he can outline the tuning knobs we typically use for bioscience corpora.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0136

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (200 prompts), baseline_benchmarks.csv
From: Sarah Jackson <sarah.jackson@acmebio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: David Harris <david.harris@acmebio.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: grounding checklist, retriever choices & eval assets for Acme BioSystems

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data sensitivity: the instrument manuals contain serial numbers and vendor PII. We will provide redacted versions for the first pass. Is the VPC option scoped for FedRAMP? If not, we need to confirm encryption-at-rest + KMS integration.

2) Retriever / index: our infra team prefers Milvus over FAISS because we plan to support live re-indexing with metadata filters (lot numbers). Will your hybrid config work with Milvus? If not, we want to understand tradeoffs.

3) Reranker: we like the idea of a lightweight cross-encoder for cost reasons — can you share a one-page on what tradeoffs we’ll see (precision vs latency)? Also curious about training data needed if we later fine-tune for assay-name disambiguation.

4) Metrics: grounding precision@1 is critical for us. For the fidelity tests, can you support a blinded review flow so our SMEs mark pass/fail without seeing model traces?

We're happy to take the prompt set and add redactions; expect that back by Thu EOD. Please confirm availability for Wed 3–4pm PT.

Best,
Sarah

--
Sarah Jackson
Director, Knowledge Systems
Acme BioSystems
sarah.jackson@acmebio.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jackson <sarah.jackson@acmebio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Harris <david.harris@acmebio.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: grounding checklist, retriever choices & eval assets for Acme BioSystems

Sarah — great questions. Short answers + attachments: I attached a short reranker-proposal.pdf that outlines performance tradeoffs.

1) VPC / compliance: our Private deployment supports KMS/HSM integrations and configurable retention. FedRAMP is not a standard offering today — we can share encryption + audit-log artifacts for your security review; Karthik can send the SOC/Security pack in a separate thread if that helps.

2) Milvus vs FAISS: Our runtime supports Milvus and FAISS backends. Hybrid BM25 + dense is an architecture pattern — the dense side can be backed by Milvus with metadata filters; BM25 runs alongside. For live re-indexing we recommend the IVF/Milvus path to keep ingests performant.

3) Reranker tradeoffs (high-level): 
   - distil-cross-enc-1.2 (cheap): good precision @ top-1 on common QA, ~2–5x faster than larger cross-encoders, minimal fine-tuning required.
   - domain-finetuned cross-encoder: +6–12% precision lift on disambiguation tasks (assay names), but expects ~300–1,000 in-domain labeled pairs and adds ~100–200ms to p95 latency unless you use a split architecture (candidate prune -> rerank). See reranker-proposal.pdf attached.

4) Blinded fidelity review: yes — we can provide a simple UI export where SMEs mark pass/fail and leave comments; no model traces shown. We'll also store hashed answers if you want to audit later.

Proposed pilot timeline (quick):
- Week 0: finalize redacted prompt set + a 500–1,000 doc sample for chunking tests.
- Week 1: index + run baseline configs (4 runs).
- Week 2: collect SME labels on the 200 prompt checks; iterate reranker if needed.

Wed 3–4pm PT works — I booked that slot and shared a Calendar invite. If David or others need a different time, let me know.

Action items for Acme: redacted prompt set + one representative manual PDF by Thu EOD (2027-04-28).

Thanks — looping Karthik to outline any tuning knobs he wants to prepare in advance.

--
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jackson <sarah.jackson@acmebio.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: David Harris <david.harris@acmebio.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: grounding checklist, retriever choices & eval assets for Acme BioSystems

Hi Sarah — quick technical notes ahead of our Wed session: 

Retriever tuning knobs I recommend we validate in the pilot:
- Chunking: try 256-token and 512-token windows with 50% overlap; procedural steps often live in short spans so smaller chunks can increase exact-match recall.
- Embedding model: text-embedding-3-small is a sensible low-cost baseline; if recall is low we run text-embedding-3-large for the dense config.
- Indexing: use Milvus IVF + HNSW for nearest-neighbor; apply metadata (document_version, lot_number) filters where you want per-lot queries.

Reranker strategy:
- Candidate generation: set k=50 for dense-only and k=20 for hybrid to keep reranker cost reasonable.
- Reranker: start with distil-cross-enc-1.2 as baseline. If we see ambiguity in assay names, plan a second-phase fine-tune using 300 labeled pairs (we can help label or provide an annotation template).

Grounding metrics to capture (we'll produce scripts):
- grounding_precision@1/3/5 (manual labels vs returned citations),
- fidelity_pass_rate (SME pass/fail),
- provenance_coverage (fraction of answers with at least one citation),
- hallucination_rate (SME-labeled free-text hallucinations per 100 queries).

I attached two quick artifacts to the Drive folder (shared in the invite): a sample eval script and an annotation template for the SME review. Please review before Wed so we can move quickly.

If you prefer, we can run an initial smoke test using a 25-prompt subset tomorrow to validate chunk size and embedding choice; tell us which 25 prompts to highlight.

See you on Wed.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
